- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.5) and model forecast is significantly below recent highs, adjust upward to avoid underestimating rebound potential.  
- If model forecast spikes sharply after a recent dip, reduce the overshoot by 10–15% to prevent overreaction.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if the last 3–5 days of true values show strong upward momentum (e.g., >+1.5% daily), model should not lag more than 2–3 days behind.  
- When sentiment is positive (especially > 0.3) and model is flat or declining, increase forecast slightly to capture sentiment-driven momentum.  
- If model consistently underestimates true values in the 10–15th day of the forecast horizon, apply a +0.5 to +1.0 unit bias correction for the next 3–5 days.  
- Avoid forecasting below 65.0 unless sentiment is strongly bearish and historical lows are confirmed.  
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly negative and true values are trending upward, model should not be more than 1.5% below the 30-day moving average of recent true values.
